biodiversity_overview.text: 25,952 GBIF occurrence records for 55 tracked species are attributed to Haryana, spanning 1875-2026.
25,839 of these records (99.6%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 26, Magnoliopsida 12, Mammalia 9, Squamata 4, Testudines 3, Amphibia 1.

threatened_species.text: 6 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: White-throated Munia (3,106), Indian Pied Starling (3,057), Indian Spot-billed Duck (2,552), Indian Thick-knee (2,325), Indian Cormorant (1,993).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 1,552 in 2016 to 167 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 0.39% of Haryana's area (13 areas intersect the state).
21.2% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (5,488 of 25,839); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), Indian Courser (0.47), Indian Desert Jird (0.41).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Haryana (equal-weight reference): cell near 28.125N 76.875E (overall rank 43, median rank across weightings 67); cell near 29.625N 76.875E (overall rank 227, median rank across weightings 246); cell near 28.875N 75.375E (overall rank 228, median rank across weightings 247).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 429 km2 (0.97% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

4.5 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (1.05% of the 2000 extent; 0.09% in 2015-2024, rank 28 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2009 (0.67 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 2.76% of land and population density is 667.4 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
31% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
